meta.title: The Messengers' Tree
meta.note: Three labels. Established: stated in the Qur'an, or in a hadith from the six books that we checked. Interpretive: from historical tradition (Ibn Ishaq, al-Tabari), which we have not been able to check against those works here. Disputed in the sources: named works differ. The label belongs to the person or fact; the line 'How we know this link' says what supports the connection to the parent. Gaps are deliberately folded — honest gaps are part of the design.
sources: Qur'an 6:84-90 — the chain of prophets from Ibrahim
Seerah: Ibn Ishaq/Ibn Hisham; History: al-Tabari
Qur'an 3:33-37; 66:12 — the family of Imran and Maryam's father
Qur'an 19:6 — Zakariya and the family of Ya'qub
Sahih al-Bukhari 2731, 2864 — the Prophet’s father and grandfather by name
Sahih al-Bukhari 3491; Sahih Muslim 2276 — Mudar, an-Nadr ibn Kinana; Kinana, Quraysh, Banu Hashim
Sahih al-Bukhari 3884; Sahih Muslim 976, 2404 — Abu Talib; the Prophet’s mother; Ali
Sahih al-Bukhari 1303, 3698; Qur'an 33:6, 33:59 — the Prophet’s household
Sahih Muslim 162 — Isa and Yahya as maternal cousins
meta.lineageWarning: Between Adam and Nuh, between Sam and Ibrahim, between Ismail and Adnan, above Adnan, and between Ya'qub and the later prophets, the names come from historical tradition and not from the Qur'an or the six books. The tree shows those generations as folded rows, not as verified lists. Where we could not check a name against the work it comes from, the row says so. Within the Prophet’s ﷺ own household, the names of his mother and of his other daughters are from tradition; that he had a mother, other daughters, a son Ibrahim and several wives is from the Qur’an or the hadith we checked. Ali’s father is named from tradition and from the way Ali is named in the hadith collections.
meta.unplacedNote: The Qur'an names these prophets but does not give their parents or place them in a line we can verify. They are listed by name with what the Qur'an says, and are not attached to any family.

nodes.name: Adam
nodes.description: The first man and first prophet; father of every soul in this tree. His two sons' story is in the Tales shelf (Qur'an 5:27-31).

nodes.name: Hawwa (Eve)
nodes.description: Mother of humanity; named in the tradition of Ibn Ishaq, not in the Qur'an's text.

nodes.name: Habil
nodes.description: One of the two sons of Adam whose offering was accepted; his brother killed him (Qur'an 5:27-30). The Qur'an does not give the sons' names; tradition calls him Habil.
nodes.lineageNote: The Qur'an says only 'Adam's two sons' (5:27); the names Habil and Qabil are from tradition.

nodes.name: Qabil
nodes.description: The brother who killed him; the Qur'an keeps him nameless and he is remembered by his deed (5:27-30). Tradition calls him Qabil.
nodes.lineageNote: The Qur'an says only 'Adam's two sons' (5:27); the names Habil and Qabil are from tradition.

nodes.name: Sheeth (Seth)
nodes.description: The righteous son through whom the prophetic line continued; named in tradition.

nodes.name: …ten generations…
nodes.description: The generations between Sheeth and Nuh are veiled; the tradition names them, the tree leaves them folded — the honest gap.

nodes.name: Nuh
nodes.description: The second father of humanity. From his three sons descend all the peoples of the earth; this tree follows Sam, through whom every prophet came.

nodes.name: Sam (Shem)
nodes.description: Nuh's son through whom the prophetic line ran.

nodes.name: Arfakhshadh
nodes.description: The chain from Sam to Ibrahim runs through the generations the historians record; carried as one folded branch.

nodes.name: …Shalikh, Abir, Faligh, Ra'u, Sarugh, Nahur…
nodes.description: The named ancestors of Ibrahim in the historians' tradition — one folded branch of named generations.

nodes.name: Ibrahim
nodes.description: The trunk of the whole tree. His two sons became two rivers: Ismail → the line of the final Prophet ﷺ; Ishaq → the line of Musa, Dawud, Sulayman, Zakariya, Yahya, and Isa.

nodes.name: Sarah
nodes.description: Mother of Ishaq; her story is bound to the birth of the second river.

nodes.name: Hajar
nodes.description: Mother of Ismail; her run between Safa and Marwah is the sa'i of every pilgrim.

nodes.name: Ismail
nodes.description: The elder son. From him: the Arabs, the guardianship of the Kaaba, and the line to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.

nodes.name: Qaydar & the sons of Ismail
nodes.description: The historians say Ismail had twelve sons who settled Arabia and that the Prophet’s ﷺ line ran through Qaydar. We did not find Ismail’s sons listed in the Qur’an or in the hadith we checked. Kept as one node.
nodes.lineageNote: Uncertain. Between Ismail and Adnan the names are from historians (Ibn Ishaq; al-Tabari). We could not read their lists here and did not find these generations in the Qur’an or in the six books, so they are folded and not shown as verified.

nodes.name: Adnan
nodes.description: The name the historians give for the ancestor where the Prophet’s ﷺ Arab line is traced back toward Ismail. Above Adnan the tree is uncertain: those generations are not in the Qur’an or in any hadith we checked.
nodes.lineageNote: Uncertain above this point. The link from Adnan up to Ismail is from the historians, not from the Qur’an or the six books, and has not been re-checked here.

nodes.name: …to Ma'add…
nodes.description: The generations the historians list between Adnan and Fihr are folded here, and we have not checked that list. What a hadith does tell us: the Prophet ﷺ was of the tribe of Mudar and of the offspring of an-Nadr ibn Kinana (Sahih al-Bukhari 3491, reported by Zaynab bint Abi Salama).
nodes.lineageNote: The names in between are from the historians and are not shown as verified; Mudar and an-Nadr ibn Kinana as ancestors of the Prophet ﷺ are in Sahih al-Bukhari 3491.

nodes.name: Fihr ibn Malik — Quraysh
nodes.description: The progenitor of Quraysh, the tribe of the Prophet's house and the keepers of the Kaaba. A hadith in Sahih Muslim (2276) says Allah chose Kinana from Ismail’s descendants, Quraysh from Kinana, Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and the Prophet ﷺ from Banu Hashim.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2276 (Wathila ibn al-Asqa’): the choosing of Kinana, Quraysh, Banu Hashim

nodes.name: Qusayy ibn Kilab
nodes.description: Gathered Quraysh into Makkah and took the keys of the Kaaba — the first lord of Makkah in the direct line.

nodes.name: Abd Manaf
nodes.description: Father of Hashim, from whom the clan took its name: Banu Hashim, the Prophet's own clan.

nodes.name: Hashim ibn Abd Manaf
nodes.description: The clan's namesake; the tradition honors him with instituting the two caravan journeys that made Makkah's wealth.
sources: Sahih Muslim 2276: Banu Hashim chosen from Quraysh

nodes.name: Abdul-Muttalib
nodes.description: The Prophet’s ﷺ grandfather. At Hunayn the Prophet ﷺ called out “I am the son of Abdul-Muttalib” (Sahih al-Bukhari 2864).
nodes.lineageNote: That Abdul-Muttalib was an ancestor of the Prophet ﷺ is in Sahih al-Bukhari 2864. His sons (Abdullah and Abu Talib) are from Ibn Ishaq/al-Tabari.

nodes.name: Abu Talib
nodes.description: The Prophet’s ﷺ uncle: as he lay dying the Prophet ﷺ called him “O my uncle” and asked him to say the testimony of faith (Sahih al-Bukhari 3884). He is named as the father of Ali by Ali’s own name, ‘ibn Abi Talib’; that this is the same uncle is from the historians and has not been re-checked here.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3884 (Musayyab ibn Hazn): Abu Talib, “O my uncle”
Sahih Muslim 2404 (Ali named ‘ibn Abi Talib’ in the chapter heading)
Ibn Ishaq (his father; his son Ali)
nodes.lineageNote: His being the Prophet’s uncle is in Sahih al-Bukhari 3884. His father (Abdul-Muttalib) and his being Ali’s father are from Ibn Ishaq/al-Tabari and the usual way Ali is named; we have not re-read those works here.

nodes.name: Abdullah ibn Abdul-Muttalib
nodes.description: The Prophet’s ﷺ father. In the Hudaybiyyah treaty the Prophet ﷺ told them to write “Muhammad bin Abdullah” (Sahih al-Bukhari 2731). That he died on a trading journey before his son was born is from the historians.
sources: Ibn Ishaq; al-Tabari (his death; his father Abdul-Muttalib)
nodes.lineageNote: The Prophet’s father’s name is in Sahih al-Bukhari 2731. That Abdullah was Abdul-Muttalib’s son is from Ibn Ishaq/al-Tabari, which we have not re-read here.

nodes.name: Amina
nodes.description: The Prophet’s ﷺ mother. A hadith says only “his mother”: he asked his Lord’s permission to visit her grave and was given it (Sahih Muslim 976). Her name, and that she was Abdullah’s wife, are from Ibn Ishaq and have not been re-checked here.
sources: Sahih Muslim 976 (Abu Huraira): his mother’s grave
nodes.lineageNote: A mother is in Sahih Muslim 976; her name and marriage to Abdullah are from tradition.

nodes.name: Muhammad ﷺ
nodes.description: The Seal of the Prophets — the first river of Ibrahim’s house reaching its ocean. In the Hudaybiyyah treaty he had himself written as “Muhammad bin Abdullah” (Sahih al-Bukhari 2731). Read his life in the Seerah shelf.
nodes.lineageNote: His father’s name is in Sahih al-Bukhari 2731; the line above his father to Adnan is from the historians and is uncertain above Adnan.

nodes.name: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid
nodes.description: The first to believe; mother of Fatima. Her portrait is in the Women shelf.

nodes.name: His other wives — the Mothers of the Believers
nodes.description: The Qur’an says the Prophet’s ﷺ wives are in the position of the believers’ mothers (33:6) and speaks to them directly (33:28-34). Several have their own portrait in the Women shelf: Aisha, Hafsa, Zaynab bint Jahsh, Umm Salama, Juwayriyya and Safiyya. They are folded into one node here; we do not give an order of marriages.

nodes.name: Fatima al-Zahra
nodes.description: The leader of the women of Paradise. Her portrait is in the Women shelf.

nodes.name: His other daughters
nodes.description: The Qur’an speaks of the Prophet’s ﷺ “daughters”, in the plural (33:59). A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari (3698) says a daughter of the Prophet ﷺ was Uthman’s wife and was ill when Badr was fought. The names the tradition gives (Zaynab, Ruqayya, Umm Kulthum) are from the historians and have not been re-checked here.
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3698 (Uthman ibn Mawhab, from Ibn Umar)
nodes.lineageNote: That he had daughters besides Fatima is in the Qur’an (33:59) and Sahih al-Bukhari 3698; their names and their mother are from tradition.

nodes.name: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ﷺ
nodes.description: The Prophet’s ﷺ young son. Anas saw the Prophet ﷺ take him, kiss him and smell him, and weep when he died, saying the eyes shed tears and the heart grieves (Sahih al-Bukhari 1303; Sahih Muslim 2315).
nodes.lineageNote: The report calls him the Prophet’s son; it does not name his mother.

nodes.name: Hasan & Husayn
nodes.description: The leaders of the youth of Paradise — the Prophet's ﷺ two grandsons, loved by the whole ummah.

nodes.name: Ali ibn Abi Talib
nodes.description: The Prophet’s ﷺ cousin and son-in-law; husband of Fatima. The Prophet ﷺ told him that he stood to him as Harun stood to Musa, except that there is no prophet after him (Sahih Muslim 2404). His portrait is in the Companions shelf.
sources: Tradition: Ali son of Abu Talib
nodes.lineageNote: Ali is called ‘ibn Abi Talib’ in the hadith collections (for example the chapter heading of Sahih Muslim 2404). That his father is the Prophet’s uncle of Sahih al-Bukhari 3884 is from the historians and has not been re-checked here.

nodes.name: Ishaq
nodes.description: The second son — through him the prophetic line ran into the tribes of Israel and to every prophet after him until Isa.

nodes.name: Ya'qub (Israel)
nodes.description: Israel — father of twelve sons, the twelve tribes. From his line: Musa, Dawud, Sulayman, Zakariya, Yahya, Isa.
nodes.lineageNote: That Musa, Dawud and Isa were sent to, or came from, the Children of Israel is in the Qur'an (17:2; 2:246; 5:78). The generations that connect each of them to Ya'qub are from tradition and are folded in this tree.

nodes.name: Yusuf
nodes.description: The beloved son — the best of stories is in the Prophets shelf.

nodes.name: Binyamin
nodes.description: Yusuf's younger brother. The Qur'an speaks of 'a brother of yours from your father' and 'his brother' (12:59, 12:69) and never names him; tradition calls him Binyamin.
nodes.lineageNote: Yusuf's brother is in the Qur'an; the name is from tradition.

nodes.name: …the generations to Musa's father…
nodes.description: The Qur'an places Musa among the Children of Israel, Ya'qub's descendants (17:2), but names neither his father nor his ancestors. Tradition supplies the generations; they are folded here.
nodes.lineageNote: Folded: the Qur'an gives no generations here.

nodes.name: Imran (Amram) — Musa's father, by tradition
nodes.description: Musa's father in the tradition's lists. The Qur'an does not name Musa's father. The Imran the Qur'an names (3:33-35; 66:12) is Maryam's father, and the Qur'an does not say he is Musa's father, so this tree keeps them as two separate nodes.
nodes.lineageNote: Musa's father is named only by tradition.

nodes.name: Musa & Harun
nodes.description: The two brothers of the exodus — Musa, who spoke to Allah, and Harun, his support. Both in the Prophets shelf.

nodes.name: The Line of Dawud
nodes.description: Dawud and Sulayman rose from Ya'qub's line in the generations after Musa — the historians carry the names; the Qur'an carries the glory.

nodes.name: Dawud
nodes.description: The king-psalmist — given the Zabur, the echoing mountains, the pliable iron. In the Prophets shelf.

nodes.name: Sulayman
nodes.description: The kingdom no one will have after him. In the Prophets shelf.

nodes.name: …the generations to Zakariya…
nodes.description: Zakariya prays for an heir 'who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub' (19:6), so the Qur'an ties him to Ya'qub's family. It does not list the generations; tradition does, and they are folded here.
nodes.lineageNote: Qur'an 19:6 ties him to the family of Ya'qub; the generations are from tradition.

nodes.name: …the generations to Maryam's father…
nodes.description: Maryam belongs to the Children of Israel: her son is sent to them (3:49). The Qur'an gives no generations between Ya'qub and her father Imran. Tradition supplies lists; they are folded here and not relied on.
nodes.lineageNote: Folded: the Qur'an gives the family of Imran (3:33) but not the generations before him.

nodes.name: Imran, father of Maryam
nodes.description: The Qur'an calls Maryam 'daughter of Imran' (66:12) and names 'the family of Imran' among those Allah chose (3:33). His wife made the vow of 3:35.
nodes.lineageNote: Stated in the Qur'an (66:12).

nodes.name: The wife of Imran
nodes.description: She pledged the child in her womb to Allah (3:35) and, when a girl was born, named her Maryam (3:36). The Qur'an does not give her own name.
nodes.lineageNote: Stated in the Qur'an (3:35-36); her own name is not given there.

nodes.name: Zakariya
nodes.description: The guardian of Maryam (3:37), given Yahya in old age; his supplication is preserved (3:38; 19:2-6; 21:89). He was her guardian; the Qur'an does not make him her father or husband.
nodes.lineageNote: His tie to Ya'qub's family is in his own prayer (19:6).

nodes.name: Yahya
nodes.description: The son given to the barren house — 'Yahya, confirming a word from Allah' (3:39).
sources: Sahih Muslim 162 (Anas): Isa and Yahya, cousins on their mothers’ side

nodes.name: Maryam bint Imran
nodes.description: Chosen above the women of the worlds, mother of Isa without a father. The Qur'an calls her daughter of Imran (66:12) and her guardian was Zakariya (3:37). Her portrait is in the Women shelf.
nodes.lineageNote: Her father and mother are in the Qur'an (3:35; 66:12); Zakariya was her guardian, not her parent.

nodes.name: Isa
nodes.description: The final prophet of the second river — a word from Allah, raised to Him, and returning. In the Prophets shelf.
sources: Sahih Muslim 162 (Anas): Isa and Yahya, cousins on their mothers’ side
nodes.lineageNote: The Qur'an gives Isa no father (3:47; 19:20-21); he is called the son of Maryam.

nodes.name: Hud
nodes.description: Sent to the people of 'Ad as 'their brother' (7:65), meaning one of their own people. The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Salih
nodes.description: Sent to the people of Thamud as 'their brother' (7:73), meaning one of their own people; the she-camel was the sign. The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Shu'ayb
nodes.description: Sent to the people of Madyan as 'their brother' (7:85), calling them to full measure and weight. The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Lut (Lot)
nodes.description: He believed Ibrahim (29:26) and was sent to his own people (29:28-30). The Qur'an does not say how he was related to Ibrahim, so he is not attached to Ibrahim's line here. The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Idris
nodes.description: 'A man of truth and a prophet'; Allah 'raised him to a high station' (19:56-57), and he is counted among the patient (21:85). The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Ayyub (Job)
nodes.description: Called on his Lord in affliction and was answered; his family was given back to him (21:83-84; 38:41-44). The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Yunus (Jonah)
nodes.description: One of the messengers (37:139); the story of the ship and the fish is in 37:140-148 and his supplication in 21:87-88. The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Ilyas (Elias)
nodes.description: One of the messengers, who asked his people why they called on Ba'l (37:123-125); counted among the righteous (6:85). The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Al-Yasa' (Elisha)
nodes.description: Named among those Allah preferred over the worlds (6:86) and among the outstanding (38:48). The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.

nodes.name: Dhul-Kifl
nodes.description: Named among the patient (21:85-86) and among the outstanding (38:48). The Qur'an gives no parents. Not attached to any family here.
nodes.lineageNote: Not given in the Qur'an; no parent is guessed.
